rationale: The Lewy body dementia report analyzes biomarkers in a trial subset. Visual hallucinations appear in the clinical background, with no attack frequency or dried-fig exposure measured in this analysis.
Drooling occurs in a described genetic dyskinesia attack in children. The paper has neither a Parkinson sialorrhea comparison nor a raw-fig exposure.
The dental case discusses salivary dysregulation and dry mouth in Parkinson disease. It does not measure drooling severity or compare raw figs.
Orange denotes an illustration color. The clinical case series does not count Parkinson falls or evaluate consumption of oranges.
Three dystonia observations refer to a diagnostic comparator group. The paper has no fresh-sage exposure or dystonia-severity response.
A Parkinson case describes less dystonia during a change to dopaminergic treatment. It provides a clinical symptom observation without fresh-sage exposure or an independent control.
The Parkinson diary cohort records off-dose dystonia at baseline in 17 of 28 participants. Rater agreement concerns motor states and supplies no fresh-sage or dystonia-severity response.

The effort task includes Parkinson rigidity scores in alternate models. The separate supplement reports the rigidity by effort-ratio term at p=0.054. These are clinical covariates, with no dried-sage or rigidity treatment comparison.
A Parkinson postoperative case reports a transient rigidity observation in the context of a clinical complication. The case has no dried-sage exposure.
The registry compares post-fracture care outcomes. It does not measure rigidity severity or exposure to dried sage.

The OPTI-ON supplement reports NoMoFa pain improvement for 34 of 116, 30 of 99 and 33 of 100 assessed participants at one, three and six months. The uncontrolled medication cohort does not compare dried dates.

The prospective Gaucher cohort assesses sensory and nonmotor symptoms. Pain appears in the miscellaneous domain of the clinical scale, without a dried-date comparison or Parkinson pain-intensity result.

The scoping review traces hand pain and related function observations to clinical interventions and partly overlapping case series. It supplies secondary clinical context without a dried-date contrast.
The case mentions truncal muscle pain in the clinical history and dental discomfort assessment. It does not supply a change in Parkinson pain severity or a dried-date exposure.

The safinamide narrative identifies separate primary reports using pain-treatment use, bodily discomfort and a dedicated Parkinson pain scale. It contains no dried-date comparison or independent clinical cohort.
The protocol plans an executive-function comparison and secondary cognitive measures. Dried dates and a dedicated pain-intensity outcome are absent.
The frontotemporal dementia case supplies a behavioral and genetic assessment. It does not measure a Parkinson pain response to dried dates.
Bodily pain is an item domain in a multiple sclerosis quality-of-life tool. This is a protocol with no Parkinson pain result or dried-date intervention.
Pain appears as background for the polyneuropathy comparator. The study measures choice behavior by medication state in Parkinson disease and does not evaluate dried dates.
Rest tremor appears as a clinical feature of Lewy body dementia in a biomarker analysis. The analysis does not measure rest-tremor response or compare raw figs.
The review concerns striatal hand deformity and diagnosis or treatment. It has no separate raw-fig rest-tremor comparison.

OPTI-ON Supplementary Table S5 records clinician-rated apathy improvement in 12 of 65 at three months and 25 of 117 at six months. The uncontrolled Parkinson medication cohort did not compare dried dates.
The Gaucher cohort reports repeated Non-Motor Symptoms Scale outcomes including a composite mood/apathy domain. This is not an isolated Parkinson apathy or dried-date comparison.
The medication review has no original cohort or dedicated dried-date apathy outcome.
The active study protocol compares magnetic stimulation and sham on executive function. It contains no dried-date or standalone apathy outcome.
A caregiver's report of persistent apathy is part of the frontotemporal dementia case's rated behavioral history. It is clinical context from another disease without a dried-date contrast.
The Parkinson depression protocol discussion mentions apathy as one feature. No separately measured apathy result or dried-date comparison is reported.

The study compares directed exploration after assignment to different medication states in Parkinson disease. Apathy is invoked as an interpretation of choice behavior, without an independent apathy response or dried dates.
An olfactory assessment supplies a clinical predictor in a Parkinson mild cognitive impairment model. The model does not measure change in smell after fresh sage.
Hyposmia is included among diagnostic histories outside a food intervention, without objective confirmation in every case. No fresh-sage contrast is present.
The Parkinson cohort records questionnaire-reported fall history. The paper predicts cognitive classification and supplies neither prospective fall frequency nor dried-sage exposure.
Alzheimer disease was compared with a clinical control on strength measurements. Fall risk is contextual, and neither falls nor dried-sage exposure were measured.
The clinical case describes a postoperative neurologic event and symptom changes. It supplies neither a fall-frequency outcome nor a dried-sage comparison.
Most selected hip fractures followed low falls. The study compares outcomes after fracture, without longitudinal fall counts or a dried-sage intervention.
Fatigue is discussed as a barrier to exercise. The coaching study measures self-efficacy and well-being and does not evaluate fresh sage.
Transient drowsiness is reported during a change in clinical treatment. There is no dedicated fatigue measure or fresh-sage exposure.
Diary ratings compare timing of motor states. The Parkinson study does not assess fatigue severity or evaluate fresh sage.
Torque and work measurements in Alzheimer disease assess muscle strength. The study has no clinical fatigue outcome or sage exposure.
The coaching study discusses apathy as a possible barrier and uses self-efficacy and well-being outcomes. It reports no isolated apathy result or dried-sage exposure.

The effort-choice study measures baseline apathy separately. Supplementary Table 2 reports an interaction of Apathy Evaluation Scale score and effort ratio, p=0.003, for choice behavior. No dried-sage exposure or apathy response was measured.
